title: What if a term depends on the two terms before it?
description: In the list three, four, seven, eleven, eighteen, each term is the sum of the two terms before it. The video uses this to find the next term, and Keeko's doubt, that the jumps grow by one, is broken.
teaching_notes: One idea: a rule can use earlier terms, not only a fixed or growing jump. Watch for students who keep looking at jumps after the jumps have stopped helping.

video_script.why: The child sees that a rule can combine earlier terms, and uses the sum of the last two terms to find the next one.
video_script.substitution: Each term is the sum of the two terms before it.
video_script.anchor: a row of five number cards 3, 4, 7, 11, 18 with arcs from each pair of neighbours to the card that follows them
video_script.wrong_answer: the jumps go up by one each time
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says the jumps go up by one each time, as in the last list. The jumps here are one, three, four and seven, and they do not grow by one, so the doubt is struck.
video_script.payoff_line: The next term is twenty nine

final_answer.spoken: the next term is twenty nine

never_show: the jumps go up by 1 each time
maths_rules: the rule: each term is the sum of the two terms before it
slip: the jumps here are 1, 3, 4, 7, which do not grow by 1
video_script.design: One idea: a term can be the sum of the two terms before it. Assumes finding a jump. Wrong idea: the jumps always grow by one. The cards stay on the board to the end.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; five number cards in a row: 3, 4, 7, 11, 18

marks.book: the title card From your book appears
marks.cards: the five number cards appear one by one
marks.ask: a question mark card appears after the last number

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about a list of numbers.
<bookmark mark='cards'/>It begins three, four, seven, eleven, eighteen.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Which number comes next in this list?

beats.on_screen: the cards hold still and the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

beats.on_screen: two cards joined by an arc to a third card; the label sum appears on the arc

marks.arc: an arc joins two neighbouring cards to the card after them
marks.sum: the word sum is written on the arc

narration: <bookmark mark='arc'/>A rule does not have to add the same number each time.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>It can use the terms that came before. The sum of two numbers is what we get when we add them.
<bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the terms three, four, seven, eleven and eighteen.

marks.find: the words the next term are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the next term.

beats.on_screen: Step 1, look at the two terms before each term: 3 + 4 = 7, 4 + 7 = 11, 7 + 11 = 18

marks.sums: an arc from each pair of neighbours to the next term is labelled with its sum

narration: <bookmark mark='sums'/>Step one, look at the two terms before each term. Three plus four is seven, and four plus seven is eleven. Seven plus eleven is eighteen.

beats.on_screen: Step 2, the rule: each term is the sum of the two terms before it

marks.rule: the rule is written under the arcs

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>Step two, write the rule. Each term is the sum of the two terms before it.

beats.on_screen: Step 3, add the last two terms: 11 + 18 = 29

marks.next: a new card appears after eighteen with 29 on it

narration: <bookmark mark='next'/>Step three, add the last two terms of the list. Eleven plus eighteen is twenty nine.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The next term is twenty nine, the sum of the two terms before it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the boxed answer
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's doubt in a bubble; the jumps 1, 3, 4, 7 are written under the cards and do not grow by the same amount; the bubble is struck through

marks.jumps: the jumps 1, 3, 4, 7 are written under the cards
marks.fix: the bubble is struck through and the arcs glow

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the jumps go up by one each time, as they did in the last list.
<bookmark mark='jumps'/>But the jumps here are one, three, four and seven, and they do not grow by one.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>When the jumps stop helping, look at the terms before.
